claims.question: q2
claims.claim: A common RAG approach converts a text corpus into word embeddings.
claims.quote: For many practitioners, this means taking a corpus of text and converting it to a series of word embeddings.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Knowledge graph data still suffers from garbage-in, garbage-out problems.
claims.quote: However, like many cases in data science, the data associated with knowledge graphs still suffer from the problem of GIGO: “garbage in, garbage out.”

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Lack of quality entity resolution is a common source of data garbage, especially for knowledge graphs.
claims.quote: One of the most common sources of data “garbage,” which is particularly true for knowledge graphs, is lack of quality entity resolution.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The author states that regex and edit distance cannot resolve a hard identity case involving name variants and shared identifiers.
claims.quote: No RegEx in the world is going to save you in this case! Neither will an edit distance algorithm.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Kroger operates grocery stores under its own name and also owns City Market, Smith’s, and Harris Teeter.
claims.quote: For example, consider the retail company of Kroger. They operate many grocery stores called “Kroger,” but they also own a variety of other stores including City Market, Smith’s, and Harris Teeter, to name a few.
